items.title: Nebius revenue surges but capacity delays and higher spending pressure AI-cloud shares
items.summary: Nebius reported third-quarter revenue of $980.8 million, up 571% year over year, but now expects 2026 sales at the low end of its prior range after third-party capacity was delayed. Its spending forecast rose to roughly $27 billion, weighing on premarket shares. Contract retention is encouraging; deployment timing, financing and cash generation remain key risks.

observations.label: Q3 reported November 12
observations.value: Revenue $980.8 million (+571% year-on-year); adjusted EBITDA $465.8 million; net loss from continuing operations $37.5 million

observations.label: 2026 outlook and capacity
observations.value: Revenue expected at low end of $3.0-$3.4 billion; some third-party capacity pushed into H1 2027

observations.label: 2026-2027 capital spending plans
observations.value: 2026 capex around $27 billion versus prior $20-$25 billion; 2027 projected $40-$45 billion, subject to financing and execution

observations.label: Premarket response, November 12
observations.value: Reuters reported NBIS down nearly 12% at 7:16 AM ET; another morning report indicated about -8.3%; both are changing premarket indications

observations.label: What to watch
observations.value: Customer prepayments, contracted capacity delivery dates, funding costs, revised revenue pace and evidence of 2027 pre-tax breakeven

items.key_finding: Exceptional AI cloud demand is not preventing execution delays or a higher capital burden.

sources.title: Reuters November 12 capacity-delay and spending report

items.title: Fermi jumps on $200 million AI-campus prepayment, but 600 MW long-term lease is unsigned
items.summary: Fermi reported a roughly 18% premarket jump after an unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler agreed to a $200 million prepayment toward its 600 MW Texas AI-campus buildout. It remains pre-revenue and posted a $141.6 million Q3 loss, while a previous TensorWave lease and AMD support ended. A definitive new lease and dependable financing remain the tests.

observations.label: Customer commitments, November 12
observations.value: $200 million prepayment toward 600 MW starting 2027; $15 million early construction agreement; $90 million materials agreement being finalized

observations.label: Market reaction, November 12 premarket
observations.value: FRMI up around 18% according to Barron's; premarket observation, not confirmed close

observations.label: Lease qualification
observations.value: Customer unnamed; long-term lease not yet signed; earlier TensorWave lease and related AMD credit support terminated

observations.label: Q3 balance and results
observations.value: Net loss $141.6 million; $315.5 million cash and restricted cash; $958.4 million outstanding net debt

observations.label: Watch/invalidation
observations.value: Signed lease, power delivery milestones, counterparty commitments, new equity/debt financing and site permitting

items.key_finding: An upfront payment offers tangible demand evidence, but Fermi is still pre-lease and capital intensive.

sources.title: Fermi November 12 earnings and hyperscaler announcement

items.title: China approves Eli Lilly's oral weight-loss medicine orforglipron
items.summary: China's medicine regulator approved Lilly's oral GLP-1 weight-management medicine on November 12, a significant regulatory expansion in a large obesity market. Early premarket reporting put LLY up around 2.8%, though quotes were fluid. The commercial impact depends on launch timing, pricing, reimbursement, competition, and supply.

observations.label: Regulatory decision, November 12
observations.value: China National Medical Products Administration approved orforglipron for weight management in adults

observations.label: Premarket response, November 12 at 5:07 AM ET report
observations.value: Investing.com reported LLY around +2.8%; not a closing price

observations.label: Commercial opportunity
observations.value: Oral small-molecule GLP-1 option in China alongside established injectable products; Novo Nordisk oral Wegovy application remains a competitor

observations.label: Watch/invalidation
observations.value: Official label, launch date, reimbursement, access, supply and actual prescription uptake

items.key_finding: The China approval is confirmed, while its sales impact and sustained price response are not.

sources.title: China Daily Business News November 12 regulator report

items.title: Nvidia leadership crisis drives roughly 7% premarket slide and global chip pressure
items.summary: Nvidia dropped roughly 7% in early Thursday trading after Reuters confirmed its board met to consider CEO Jensen Huang's future. No removal has been announced. Founder-dependence, China export scrutiny and AI-infrastructure financing amplify the spillover risk; a formal board decision would be the next decisive signal.

observations.label: NVDA early Thursday trading
observations.value: Approximately -7% premarket/Frankfurt; intraday indication, not an official close

observations.label: Asian equity spillover
observations.value: Taiwan benchmark -2.6%; MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan -1.2% in Reuters early-November-12 report

observations.label: Leadership status
observations.value: Reuters confirmed board met November 11; no dismissal announcement verified

observations.label: Fundamental assessment / risk
observations.value: Nvidia retains a critical AI-compute franchise, but concentrated leadership and export controls threaten execution and customers' infrastructure plans

observations.label: Next indicators
observations.value: Official board/company statement, SEC disclosure, export rules, US open and chip-sector breadth

items.key_finding: An unconfirmed leadership outcome is producing a confirmed cross-market risk signal, not a fundamental-demand collapse.

sources.title: Reuters, Nvidia board weighs CEO Huang's future, November 12
Reuters, global stocks and rates, November 12

items.title: Verified VLCC strike injures four in Gulf as Hormuz attacks persist despite softer crude
items.summary: India's shipping minister confirmed a projectile hit VLCC Fujairah Energy on November 10, injuring four crew members. Maritime reporting identifies other November 10–11 tanker incidents, with some details still preliminary. This is physical shipping disruption rather than a market rumor, even as oil prices soften on hopes of diplomacy.

observations.label: Confirmed vessel incident
observations.value: MT Fujairah Energy struck November 10 en route Al Ruwais to Dubai; four of 22 crew injured; Indian shipping minister reported November 11

observations.label: Other vessel reports
observations.value: Seatrade Maritime reports Sea 1 hit November 10 and possible NCC Fajr incident November 11; details vary in certainty

observations.label: Thursday crude price observation
observations.value: WSJ reported front-month Brent $91.79 (-1%) and WTI $85.69 (-1%) early November 12; not settlement

observations.label: Safety authority context
observations.value: IMO November 11 statement reports more than 130 attacks on commercial shipping in and around Hormuz during the conflict

observations.label: Next indicators / invalidation
observations.value: UKMTO notices, verified tanker transits and exports, additional vessel damage, US-Iran negotiations, EIA petroleum data noon ET

items.key_finding: Physical-flow risk remains elevated even though oil prices are repricing diplomatic optimism.

sources.title: India minister report via Anadolu Agency, November 11
Wall Street Journal, oil and Iran talks November 12
